title: Modelled road-salt loads did not predict lower calling detection of salt-sensitive frogs than of salt-tolerant frogs at NAAMP stops in the eastern and central US in 2001-2015
abstract: Question: do salt-sensitive anurans have lower calling detection where and when more road de-icing salt is applied, relative to salt-tolerant anurans at the same roadside stops? Data: North American Amphibian Monitoring Program (NAAMP) stop records 2001-2015 (189,679 stop-runs, 11,963 stops, 1,176 routes; USGS, public domain), USGS annual 1-km road-salt estimates (Bock et al., ver. 2.0), and GHCN-CAMS winter temperature. Design (plan written before the fits): a-priori classes from field and toxicity studies (sensitive: wood frog, pickerel frog; tolerant: green frog, American toad, bullfrog, northern leopard frog); stop-run linear probability models per species x region with day, air temperature, wind, traffic noise, car count and winter anomaly terms; route-clustered errors; class contrasts from route influence functions. Primary test (time): stop and state x year fixed effects, salt of the three preceding years. In NE, MW and mid-Atlantic salt states (801 routes) the sensitive-minus-tolerant contrast was -0.18 percentage points per 10 t/km2 (95% CI -2.20 to +1.85); within-state exposure permutation p = 0.92; next-year placebo null. The planned decision rule was not met. In space (route x year effects), detection of both classes was lower at stops with more salt and roads (-0.87 and -0.85 points per log unit); the contrast was -1.1% of mean detection (CI -7.7% to +5.6%). Traffic noise lowered detection of both classes by 12-13%; noise and car terms removed about 30% of the naive spatial slope. A trend term was opposite to a salt-damage expectation (sensitive species gained at high-salt stops, +1.37 points per 10 t/km2 per decade, CI +0.30 to +2.45; descriptive). Limitations: the salt data are a deterministic allocation of state totals by road density and snowfall normal, so salt and roads cannot be separated in space and the year-to-year variation is small (SD 0.35-0.88 t/km2); detection at a stop is not pond occupancy; no measured chloride; data end in 2015.

display.caption: Unit slopes of stop calling detection (95% route-clustered CI) for salt in the three preceding years (Test B, stop and state x year fixed effects), for next-year salt (placebo), and for log(1 + mean stop salt) within route x year (Test A). Orange: a-priori salt-sensitive species; blue: salt-tolerant; grey: intermediate (not in contrasts). Black diamonds: pooled sensitive-minus-tolerant contrast in NE+MW+MA.
